name: Serua
title: Mother of Jeroboam
summary: Serua (also called Seruja) was a widow who was the mother of Jeroboam, the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel after the division of the realm. She is known primarily through her son, who became a central figure in Israel's history. The Bible mentions her briefly as Jeroboam's mother in connection with his rebellion against King Solomon.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Jeroboam's mother
keyEvents.description: Serua is introduced in the Bible as a widow and the mother of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who raised his hand against King Solomon.

keyEvents.title: Jeroboam's rebellion against Solomon
keyEvents.description: Her son Jeroboam, a capable man whom Solomon had put in charge, rebelled against the king. This led to a pivotal event in Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: The prophet Ahijah's promise to Jeroboam
keyEvents.description: The prophet Ahijah from Shiloh gave Jeroboam the promise that he would become king over ten of the tribes of Israel, which directly affected the fate of Serua's descendants.

keyEvents.title: Jeroboam Becomes King over Israel
keyEvents.description: After Solomon's death and Rehoboam's unwise rule, Jeroboam son of Seraiah was chosen king over the ten northern tribes, and the kingdom was divided.

keyEvents.title: Reference in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Seraiah is mentioned again in Chronicles in connection with Jeroboam's rebellion against Rehoboam, Solomon's son.
